candidates.exact_span:
All bulk sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, a
       reclamation site, or lawn or home garden shall be treated by either Class A or Class B pathogen
       reduction requirements as defined above in Element 1, Section I.B.3.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The land-use scope ('applied to' which site types) and the Class A versus Class B choice, resolved via cross-reference to Element 1 Section I.B.3, determine which pathogen-related requirements are applicable and what monitoring or limit comparisons are in scope.

candidates.exact_span:
a. Bulk sewage sludge shall not be applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, or a
          reclamation site that is flooded, frozen, or snow-covered so that the bulk sewage sludge
          enters a wetland or other waters of the U.S., as defined in 40 CFR 122.2, except as provided
          in a permit issued pursuant to section 404 of the CWA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of flooded/frozen/snow-covered prohibitions, the 'waters of the U.S.' definition, and the section 404 permit exception affects when application-related obligations apply, when monitoring during prohibited periods is required, and whether periods without discharge are documented conditions versus unresolved gaps.

candidates.exact_span: b. Bulk sewage sludge shall not be applied within 10 meters of a water of the U.S.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 10-meter setback requirement is a site-condition constraint whose applicability (and any associated monitoring or demonstration of compliance) depends on interpreting proximity to 'a water of the U.S.'

candidates.exact_span:
c. Bulk sewage sludge shall be applied at or below the agronomic rate in accordance with
          recommendations from the following references:
candidates.computation_change_reason: The agronomic-rate ceiling may cap applicable loading below Table 2 numeric limits; interpretation of 'agronomic rate' and which referenced guidance governs changes the effective limit for exceedance analysis and the monitoring needed to demonstrate compliance.

candidates.exact_span:    Recommendations of local extension services or Soil Conservation Services.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Multiple permissible reference sources for agronomic-rate calculations can yield different applicable loading ceilings and different evidence requirements to establish which rate was used.

candidates.exact_span:    Recommendations of a major University's Agronomic Department.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Allowing university agronomic recommendations as an alternative basis for rate determination introduces discretion over the governing standard, which can change the computed applicable limit and associated monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span:
   A statement that application of the sewage sludge to the land is prohibited except in
               accordance with the instructions on the label or information sheet.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditional prohibition ties lawful application to label or information-sheet instructions; interpretation affects whether monitoring or reporting was required to document compliant application and how missing documentation is classified versus unresolved noncompliance.
